Beentje & J.Dransf. (1995) - homotypic * ''Areca flavescens'' Voss * ''Chrysalidocarpus baronii'' var. ''littoralis'' Jum. & H.Perrier * ''Chrysalidocarpus glaucescens'' Waby |synonyms_ref = }} '''''Chrysalidocarpus lutescens''''', also known by its synonym ''Dypsis lutescens''{{cite taxon |POWO |id=665962-1 |title=''Chrysalidocarpus lutescens'' H.Wendl. |access-date=23 July 2024}} and as '''golden cane palm''', '''[[areca]] palm''', '''yellow palm''', '''butterfly palm''', or '''bamboo palm''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Arecaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to [[Madagascar]] and naturalized in the [[Andaman Islands]], [[Thailand]], [[Vietnam]], [[Réunion]], [[El Salvador]], [[Cuba]], [[Puerto Rico]], the [[Canary Islands]], southern [[Florida]], [[Haiti]], the [[Dominican Republic]], [[Jamaica]], the [[Leeward Islands]], and the [[Leeward Antilles]].{{GRIN | accessdate = 2010-12-25}} Its native names are ''rehazo'' and ''lafahazo'' (from [[Malagasy language|Malagasy]] ''hazo'' "tree" with ''reha'' "pride" and ''lafa'' "fibre", respectively).{{Cite dictionary |title=''Chrysalidocarpus lutescens'' H.Wendl. |dictionary=Dictionnaire des noms malgaches de végétaux |publisher=Editions Alzieu |url= |date=1999 |author-link=Pierre Boiteau |volume=I |page=196 |language=fr |quote=
[– lafahazo]: de lafa et hazo : arbre, donc : « arbre à crin végétal »...
[– rehazo]: de reha : fierté, orgueil; et hazo : arbre; arbre orgueilleux, de port altier... |first1=Pierre |last1=Boiteau |via=}}{{cite book |last1=Dransfield |first1=John |last2=Beentje |first2=Henk |last3=Britt |first3=Adam |last4=Ranarivelo |first4=Tianjanahary |last5=Razafitsalama |first5=Jérémie |year=2006 |url=https://kew.iro.bl.uk/downloads/d2e35b7d-713c-481a-8c40-1a7ae2c93322 |title=Field guide to the palms of Madagascar |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens |location=Kew |pages=84–85 |isbn=978-1-84246-157-0}} ==Description== ''Chrysalidocarpus lutescens'' is a perennial tropical plant that grows to {{convert|6|-|12|m|0|abbr=on}} in height and spreads from 3–5 m (8–15 ft). Multiple cane-like stems emerge from the base, creating a vase-like shape. The leaves are upward-arching, {{convert|2|-|3|m|0|abbr=on}} long, and [[pinnate]], with a yellow midrib. The [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] is yellow-green in colour and waxy in texture, with a maculate base. The leaves have 40-60 pairs of [[Leaflet (botany)|leaflets]]. Leaflet arrangement is opposite and their shape is linear to [[Glossary of leaf morphology|lanceolate]]. It bears 2-ft-long [[panicles]] of yellow flowers in summer. [[Offset (botany)|Offset]]s can be cut off when mature enough, as a [[plant propagation|propagation]] method. It bears oblong fruit that is 0.5 in long and ripens from yellow/gold to dark purple/black.{{Cite web |title=Dypsis lutescens (Areca Palm, Bamboo Palm, Butterfly Palm, Cane Palm, Golden Butterfly Palm, Golden Feather Palm, Yellow Palm) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/dypsis-lutescens/ |access-date=2023-03-16 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}} It is grown as an [[ornamental plant]] in gardens in tropical and subtropical regions, and elsewhere indoors as a [[houseplant]], one of the most important commercially. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web |title=''Dypsis lutescens'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/128311/Dypsis-lutescens/Details |access-date=3 June 2020 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society}}{{cite web |date=July 2017 |title=AGM Plants - Ornamental |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |access-date=6 February 2018 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |page=34}} One of several common names, "butterfly palm", refers to the leaves, which curve upwards in multiple stems to create a butterfly look.{{cite web |title=Real Palm Trees |url=http://realpalmtrees.com/palm-blog/a-e/areca-palm-dypsis-lutescens/ |work=Palm Tree General Description}} [[File:Chrysalidocarpus lutescens (Dypsis lutescens).jpg|thumb|right|A specimen located in the [[Andromeda Botanic Gardens]], [[Barbados]]]] In its introduced range, this plant acts as a supplier of fruit to some bird species that feed on it opportunistically, such as ''[[Pitangus sulphuratus]]'', ''[[Coereba flaveola]]'', and ''[[Thraupis sayaca]]'' species in Brazil.{{cite web |author=Leonardo Barros Ribeiro & Melisa Gogliath Silva |title=Comportamento alimentar das aves ''Pitangus sulphuratus'', ''Coereba flaveola'' e ''Thraupis sayaca'' em palmeiras frutificadas em área urbana |url=http://pepsic.bvs-psi.org.br/scielo.php?script=sci_arttext&pid=S1517-28052005000100004&lng=es&nrm=iso |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706161142/http://pepsic.bvs-psi.org.br/scielo.php?script=sci_arttext&pid=S1517-28052005000100004&lng=es&nrm=iso |archive-date=2011-07-06 |language=pt}} == Cultural requirements == In its native habitat of Madagascar, ''C. lutescens'' grows in moist, forested areas.{{Cite web |last=Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder |title=Dypsis lutescens |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=291457 |access-date=2023-03-09 |website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}} It grows best in rich, moist, and well-drained soils and in bright, partly shaded areas. It tolerates full sun, but long periods of direct sunlight may burn the foliage. Overfertilization results in yellowing of the leaves. It is a low-maintenance tropical plant.{{citation needed|date=June 2026}} It is winter hardy to USDA zones 10-11, and does well outdoors in warm climates with medium to high humidity. The plant is highly sensitive to cold temperatures.{{citation needed|date=June 2026}} == Pests and diseases == ''C. lutescens'' has no serious insect or disease problems. It is susceptible to [[Scale insect|scale]], [[Whitefly|whiteflies]], and [[spider mite]]s. Plants grown outdoors may be subject to phytoplasma disease of palms, which is spread by planthoppers and can cause severe yellowing. == Uses == In its native climate, the plant may be massed and used as a landscape specimen, privacy screen, or informal hedge. It can be grown as a tree or shrub. In areas of eastern Madagascar, this plant also has environmental and medicinal uses. It was once used as a source of fibre to make fishing nets. == Houseplant maintenance == ''Chrysalidocarpus lutescens'' is a popular, low-maintenance houseplant. If grown indoors, plant in a well-drained potting soil in a pot that has adequate drainage holes. The size of the pot should be twice the size of the root ball. Repotting may be necessary every 2–3 years, and size of the pot should only increase 3-4 inches compared to the size of the old pot.{{Cite web |title=3 Simple Ways to Care for an Areca Palm |url=https://www.wikihow.com/Care-for-an-Areca-Palm |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=wikiHow |language=en}} Ensure the plant is placed in an area with bright, indirect sunlight. It will thrive near a window where light is filtered, but will struggle if placed in the path of direct sun, which may cause scorching or yellowing of the foliage. If grown in areas with extreme temperatures, note that the plant will struggle in temperatures that drop below {{cvt|60|F}}.{{Cite web |title=Dypsis lutescens - Plant Finder |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=291457 |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}} This plant prefers moist soil, but cannot tolerate soggy conditions. To prevent overwatering, check the moisture level regularly and allow soil to dry out between waterings. The plant will benefit from fertilization in the summer when it is experiencing the most growth. ''C. lutescens'' prefers medium to high humidity; if the air indoors is too dry, the foliage may exhibit browning at the tips. This can be remedied with manual misting or adding a humidifier to the room.{{citation needed|date=June 2026}} This plant does not require pruning, but it may be done based on owner preference.{{citation needed|date=June 2026}} == Gallery == File:散尾葵Dypsis lutescens 20210511145013 03.jpg|Specimen located at [[National Chung Hsing University]], [[Taiwan]] File:Starr 060922-9185 Chrysalidocarpus lutescens.jpg|Light-yellow flowers of the plant File:Buah pinang hias (1).JPG|Fruit produced by the plant, with hue depending on ripeness File:Dypsis lutescens, AJT Johnsingh.jpg|Fruits may appear yellow to orange at specific stages.
